objective: Evaluate the effectiveness of the novel micro-machined sensor in augmenting SpO2 accuracy under low perfusion conditions
dependent_variables: SpO2 accuracy under low perfusion conditions
baseline: SpO2 accuracy under low perfusion conditions (n = 30) without device deployment
procedure: Recruit 60 patients with low perfusion conditions (MAP < 60 mmHg)
Randomly assign patients to either the device deployment group (n = 30) or the control group (n = 30)
Deploy the device in the device deployment group and monitor SpO2 accuracy for 1 hour
Measure SpO2 accuracy in both groups at 1 hour post-device deployment (or without device deployment in the control group)
Collect and analyze data on SpO2 accuracy and other relevant metrics
expected_result: A statistically significant increase in SpO2 accuracy under low perfusion conditions (p < 0.05) compared to the baseline condition
falsification_condition: Failure to demonstrate a statistically significant increase in SpO2 accuracy under low perfusion conditions (p < 0.05) compared to the baseline condition
sample_requirements: 60 patients with low perfusion conditions (MAP < 60 mmHg) in a controlled clinical setting
safety_constraints: Ensure patient safety and well-being throughout the experiment, with regular monitoring of vital signs and SpO2 accuracy
estimated_duration: 6 months (including recruitment, data collection, and analysis)
information_gain: Understanding the effectiveness of the novel micro-machined sensor in augmenting SpO2 accuracy under low perfusion conditions, and its potential to improve patient outcomes in critical care settings
